significance: A cluster of Shiva shrines near the sea about eleven miles east of Dwarka, built between the 7th and 10th centuries under Saindhava rule, with the phamsana-roofed temples placed in the middle of the 8th century. They mix the neo-Dravidic Maitraka manner with Nagara and early Maha-Gurjara forms.
story: Local people connect the monuments with the sage Durvasa and call the site Durvasa Rishi Ashram.
